whatItIs.text: A Greek white cheese aged in brine — crumbly, tangy, salty — traditionally at least 70% sheep's milk with up to 30% goat's.

historyNote.text: The name feta (Italian fetta, 'slice') only became widespread in the 19th century, probably for the way the cheese was sliced into barrels; since 2002 it carries EU protected status for mainland Greece and Lesbos, while similar brined cheeses across the Balkans go by other names.

howToChoose.text: Buy blocks in brine rather than pre-crumbled tubs — they stay moist and taste brighter; sheep's-milk feta is tangier and creamier than cow's-milk 'feta-style'.

storage.text: Keep submerged in its brine in the fridge, topping up with salty water if needed.

useItUp.text: Crumbling feta over anything hot is the easiest rescue; it also whips into dips, bakes into triangles with spinach, or grills until golden.

substitutions.note: creamier, less salty; no brine tang
